# Relative Sort Array.

@example 8, 5 and 1 come first in arr2's order, with their copies together; 0 and 3 are not listed and follow, smallest first.
[5,0,8,5,3,1,8]
[8,5,1]
=> [8,8,5,5,1,0,3]

@example arr2 lists every value, so its order is the whole answer.
[40,10,30,20]
[30,10,40,20]
=> [30,10,40,20]

@example Only 9 is listed; 2, 2, 4 and 7 come after it although they are smaller.
[7,2,9,2,4]
[9]
=> [9,2,2,4,7]

# A single value.
[0]
[0]
=> [0]

# 0 and 1000 both occur; 1000 is not listed and goes last.
[1000,0,500,1000,0]
[0]
=> [0,0,500,1000,1000]

# 1000 is listed first.
[0,1000,7,1000]
[1000,0]
=> [1000,1000,0,7]

# The first listed value has copies all over arr1, and other values are
# not listed.
[3,6,3,2,6,1,3]
[3,6]
=> [3,3,3,6,6,1,2]

# arr2 is in decreasing order.
[1,2,3,4,5,5,4]
[5,4,3,2,1]
=> [5,5,4,4,3,2,1]

# Unlisted values sit between listed ones and are smaller than them.
[12,4,99,4,7,12,50,0]
[12,99]
=> [12,12,99,0,4,4,7,50]

# Repeated unlisted values stay together, sorted.
[9,9,1,9,1,5]
[5]
=> [5,1,1,9,9,9]

# arr2 covers every value, in neither increasing nor decreasing order.
[2,0,1,2,0,1]
[1,2,0]
=> [1,1,2,2,0,0]

# All values equal.
[4,4,4]
[4]
=> [4,4,4]
